briefing.headline: Harbour Town dominate centrally and win the ball high; Kestrel struggle to regain territory or threaten

working.text: Harbour are controlling the game and territory: their control index is 72 and field tilt is 77.7%, showing sustained domination of the attacking areas.
They press intensely and win the ball very high, averaging turnovers at x = 50.5 m and recording 12 high regains in the opponent’s final third.
Harbour create far more chances: 2.6 xG from 14 shots with 8 on target, while completing 84 progressives and sending half their final-third entries through the centre.

not_working.text: Relying heavily on the middle risks becoming predictable: 50% of Harbour’s entries are central which opponents can crowd.
Sustaining an intense press could be costly late if it fades — their PPDA is very low at 4.6, so a rise would indicate tiring legs.
Although they dominate territory, possession sits at 57% (not overwhelming) so lapses or poor transitions could still allow Kestrel to relieve pressure.

predictions.claim: Harbour will aim to reduce Kestrel’s ability to attack through the centre by forcing Kestrel to use wider channels; Kestrel’s central channel entries will fall at least 30% by the 65th minute.
Harbour will probe the flanks more, increasing their right-side final-third entries by at least 40% as they look to exploit space away from a crowded centre.
Harbour’s press intensity will drop as legs tire, producing a PPDA increase of at least 20% for Harbour by the 65th minute.

working.text: Kestrel still favour central routes into the final third — 55.6% of their entries are down the middle — which gives them a clear plan to try to break down Harbour.
They have attempted a reasonable number of progressive passes (72) and completed 193 passes overall, showing a willingness to move the ball forward despite being outplayed.
Kestrel remain competitive in sequence and effort: they have 201 sprints and a sequence length of 4.58 actions, so work-rate is present even if results are poor.

not_working.text: They are being pressed off the ball and rarely win it high: PPDA at 11.5 is loose compared with Harbour and Kestrel have zero high regains.
Kestrel are creating far fewer chances: 0.82 xG with only one shot on target from six attempts, reflecting poor quality or disruption in the final third.
Their turnover height is very low (19.2 m) so Harbour are allowed to recover possession close to Kestrel’s goal far too often.

predictions.claim: To blunt Harbour’s central threat, Kestrel will sit more compact centrally and aim to cut Harbour’s central entries by at least 30% by the 65th minute.
Gregor Molina will drop a midfielder deeper to reduce Harbour’s high wins; Harbour’s high regains will fall by at least 30% by the 65th minute.
Kestrel will push to reclaim more of the ball and lift their share of possession by at least 10% as they send more players forward.
